newsitem.title: USA: Ill Central, union set contract options.
newsitem.headline: Ill Central, union set contract options.

text.p: The United Transportion Union (UTU) and the Illinois Central Railroad said on Wednesday they have signed an initial agreement under which UTU members would vote on three options to create a new contract.
The result of the ratification vote will be announced on January 17, 1997, the organizations said.
An agreement, which would apply only to UTU members of the ICR, would settle wage and work rule issues into the next century that have been under discussion since November 1994.

The three options are: $23-per-hour pay plus a one-time payment of $60,000 to each trainman to eliminate the productivity fund; a modified version of the recently imposed national UTU agreement, or binding arbitration, they said.
The first option would replace the mileage-based wage system with an hourly system.
If the first option were selected, the one-time payout per trainman would result in a special charge to be announced by the company, the groups said.
The second option primarily resolves wage increases.
The UTU represents about 700 trainmen throughout IC's system, or about 22 percent of IC's workforce.
Illinois Central Railroad, the main unit of Illinois Central Corp, operates a 2,600-mile freight railroad between Chicago and the Gulf of Mexico. ((--Chicago Newsdesk (312) 408-8787))
